junction.name: St Nicholas Avenue & West 125 Street, New York City

claims.text: St Nicholas Avenue & West 125 Street had 24 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 9 pedestrians injured, 3 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
These counts are St Nicholas Avenue & West 125 Street's own: the city's record places 52 of the 150 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $1.6 million a year.
11% of crashes here had “other vehicular” recorded as a contributing factor, against 4% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead and a two-wheeler was involved in 29% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 14% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.7 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $247,000 a year.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 0.4 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $128,000 a year; check on site: the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for St Nicholas Avenue, West 125 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10
Subject: Request for safety study at St Nicholas Avenue & West 125 Street - 40 crashes in 5 years

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

I am writing to ask you to carry out a safety study at the junction of St Nicholas Avenue & West 125 Street for the roads you are responsible for and to consider the fixes below.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 40 crashes, including 24 injury crashes. People hurt include 9 pedestrians injured and 3 cyclists injured, with no deaths recorded in this period. Using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the harm is valued at $1.6 million per year. This location is a city priority location.

The record shows a latest recorded safety project of a Leading Pedestrian Interval signal in 2024.

We ask you to consider, subject to site checks:

* reflective backplates on the traffic signals (Backplates with Retroreflective Borders), which is FHWA-cited and expected to prevent about 0.7 crashes per year targeting injury crashes, with harm avoided valued at $247,000 per year.
* longer yellow signal times (Yellow Change Intervals), expected to prevent about 0.4 crashes per year targeting injury crashes, with harm avoided valued at $128,000 per year, if a site check shows the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.

Please advise on your assessment and next steps for your roads at this junction.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
